Flocon is a debugging tool: once connected, the desktop can read your network calls, edit your preferences, delete files and run SQL on your databases. Keep it out of release builds.

Use debugImplementation with the -no-op twin in releaseImplementation, as in step 1. The no-op has the same API: nothing is started and no connection is made. Use flocon-no-op and the no-op of every module you use. In a shared Kotlin Multiplatform module, which has a single variant, swap the modules in the release configurations of the app:

// app/build.gradle.kts
val floconNoOps = mapOf(
    "io.github.openflocon:flocon" to "io.github.openflocon:flocon-no-op:LAST_VERSION",
    "io.github.openflocon:flocon-network-core" to "io.github.openflocon:flocon-network-core-no-op:LAST_VERSION",
    "io.github.openflocon:flocon-ktor-interceptor" to "io.github.openflocon:flocon-ktor-interceptor-no-op:LAST_VERSION",
    // ... one line per Flocon module you use
)

configurations.configureEach {
    if (name.startsWith("release")) {
        resolutionStrategy.dependencySubstitution {
            floconNoOps.forEach { (module, noOp) ->
                substitute(module(module)).using(module(noOp))
            }
        }
    }
}

The no-ops are binary compatible: code compiled against the real modules runs on them.

docs.title: Next: connect
docs.text: Run the app with Flocon Desktop open: on an Android emulator or a USB device it connects by itself. See Connect.

docs.title: Swift SDK (iOS & macOS)
docs.text:
Replace LAST_VERSION with the version shown on the badge.

Requirements: iOS 15+ or macOS 12+, Xcode 16+ (Swift 6).

Let your AI agent do it

The Flocon plugin adds the package, starts Flocon and keeps it out of release builds for you.

docs.title: 1. Add the package
docs.text:
In Xcode, choose File > Add Package Dependencies..., paste https://github.com/openflocon/FloconSwift.git, keep Up to Next Major Version from the latest release, and add the Flocon library to your app target.

With a Package.swift:

dependencies: [
    .package(url: "https://github.com/openflocon/FloconSwift.git", from: "LAST_VERSION"),
],
targets: [
    .target(name: "MyApp", dependencies: [
        .product(name: "Flocon", package: "FloconSwift"),
    ]),
]

gRPC (optional): the FloconSwiftGrpc package adds the interceptor for grpc-swift 1.26+ (1.x). Add https://github.com/openflocon/FloconSwiftGrpc.git (from the latest release) and the FloconGrpc library; it already includes Flocon. See gRPC.

Info.plist: add NSLocalNetworkUsageDescription so iOS lets the app reach your computer on the local network (a physical device shows a permission prompt the first time).

<key>NSLocalNetworkUsageDescription</key>
<string>Flocon connects to the desktop debugger on your computer.</string>

No App Transport Security exception is needed: the SDK uses wss:// and https:// with the self-signed certificate of the desktop (encrypted, not authenticated).

docs.title: 2. Start Flocon
docs.text:
Start the SDK as early as possible, then install the features you use. A feature that is not installed does nothing instead of crashing, so calls to it can stay in your code.

import Flocon

@main
struct MyApp: App {
    init() {
        #if DEBUG
        startFlocon { flocon in
            flocon.install(.network)
            flocon.install(.analytics)
            flocon.install(.database) { $0.register(displayName: "App", url: databaseURL) }
        }
        #endif
    }

    var body: some Scene {
        WindowGroup { ContentView() }
    }
}

The plugins are .network (also intercepts URLSession.shared), .analytics, .featureFlags, .tables, .preferences, .files, .database, .dashboard, .deeplinks, .timeline and .crashReporter. Those with options take a closure. Flocon.initialize() is the short form that installs all of them. Flocon.isLoggingEnabled = true, set before starting, prints what the SDK does with the [Flocon] prefix.

docs.title: Release builds
docs.text:
Flocon is a debugging tool: once connected, the desktop can read your network calls, edit your preferences, delete files and run SQL on your databases. Keep it out of release builds.

The Swift SDK has no no-op package. Wrap the start in #if DEBUG: the other calls (Flocon.analyticsPlugin, ...) do nothing until the SDK is started, so they can stay in your code. The package is still linked in release builds, but inert.

#if DEBUG
startFlocon { flocon in flocon.install(.network) }
#endif

docs.title: Next: connect
docs.text: Run the app with Flocon Desktop open: in the iOS Simulator or as a macOS app it connects by itself. On a physical device, see Connect.

docs.title: Install with the Flocon plugin
docs.text: The Flocon plugin for AI coding agents comes with the flocon-setup skill: ask your agent to set Flocon up, and it adds the SDK to your project for you, whatever the platform (Android, Kotlin Multiplatform, Swift, Flutter). The same plugin also connects the agent to the MCP server of Flocon Desktop, to debug your app afterwards.

docs.title: 1. Install the plugin
docs.text:
Claude CodeCodexCursor 
/plugin marketplace add openflocon/Flocon
/plugin install flocon@flocon

codex plugin marketplace add openflocon/Flocon

Then install flocon from the /plugins browser: it brings the Flocon MCP server and the two skills, Flocon MCP and Flocon Setup.

In the Cursor dashboard, open Plugins & MCPs → Add Marketplace → Import from Repo, paste https://github.com/openflocon/Flocon, then install flocon from Customize.

Other agents (Gemini CLI, Antigravity, VS Code...) get the MCP server but not the skills: install the SDK by hand (Kotlin, Swift, Flutter).

docs.title: 2. Ask your agent
docs.text:
Open your agent in the folder of your app and ask, in plain text:

Set up Flocon in this project. I want network and database, and it must not be in release builds.

The agent:

  1. Detects the platform from the project files: Android, Kotlin Multiplatform, Swift (.xcodeproj, Package.swift) or Flutter (pubspec.yaml).
  2. Detects the version if Flocon is already there, and picks a path: install, migrate from 1.x to 2.0, or only add the missing plugins.
  3. Adds the dependencies: debug module and -no-op twin for release in Kotlin, FloconSwift with Swift Package Manager, or flutter pub add flocon and the plugin packages.
  4. Starts Flocon in the app, and installs only the plugins the project really uses (it searches the code instead of guessing).
  5. Keeps it out of release: it inspects the real build variants and tells you exactly what it did (SDK inactive vs absent from the binary).
  6. Builds the touched targets and says what was not verified (running on a device, connection to Flocon Desktop, release build).

It works on a branch and does not touch your unrelated uncommitted changes. The same prompt migrates a Kotlin 1.x integration, see Migrating from 1.x.

docs.title: 3. Check it works
docs.text:
Run the app with Flocon Desktop open (see Connect), then ask your agent:

List my network calls.

If a tool returns nothing, the agent can tell which wiring is missing. More prompts in the Cookbook.

docs.title: 🐧 Install on Linux
docs.text:
Flocon Desktop is published on GitHub Releases as .deb and .rpm packages for both x64 and arm64.

Architecture Debian / Ubuntu Fedora / RHEL / openSUSE x64 (x86_64) Flocon-linux-x64.deb Flocon-linux-x64.rpm arm64 (aarch64) Flocon-linux-arm64.deb Flocon-linux-arm64.rpm

A portable jar is also attached (Flocon-linux-x64.jar, Flocon-linux-arm64.jar); it needs a JDK 21 to run.

docs.title: Homebrew (Linuxbrew)
docs.text:
If you use Homebrew on Linux, install the portable jar with its launcher (x64 and arm64). Homebrew installs OpenJDK 21 for you:

brew install openflocon/tap/flocon
flocon

Update it later with brew upgrade flocon. Homebrew does not install adb: see adb below.

docs.title: Debian / Ubuntu
docs.text: sudo apt install ./Flocon-linux-x64.deb      # or Flocon-linux-arm64.deb

docs.title: Fedora / RHEL
docs.text: sudo dnf install ./Flocon-linux-x64.rpm      # or Flocon-linux-arm64.rpm

docs.title: openSUSE
docs.text: sudo zypper install ./Flocon-linux-x64.rpm   # or Flocon-linux-arm64.rpm

docs.title: adb
docs.text:
Flocon Desktop uses adb to reach Android emulators and USB devices, and for screenshots, screen recordings and deeplinks. Install it separately:

sudo apt install android-tools-adb   # Debian / Ubuntu
sudo dnf install android-tools       # Fedora
sudo zypper install android-tools    # openSUSE

Flocon starts from the app menu (Development) or with /opt/flocon/bin/Flocon.

Next: add the SDK to your app.

docs.title: 🍺 Homebrew (recommended)
docs.text:
Installing with Homebrew skips the Gatekeeper prompt entirely:

brew install --cask openflocon/tap/flocon

Update with brew upgrade --cask flocon.

docs.title: 💿 DMG
docs.text:
Download the DMG of your Mac from the releases page, open it and drag Flocon.app to /Applications:

Mac File Apple silicon (M1 and later) Flocon-macos-arm64.dmg Intel Flocon-macos-x64.dmg

Because the DMG comes from GitHub Releases and not the Mac App Store, macOS Gatekeeper shows a security prompt on the first launch. Authorize the app with one of the two options below.

docs.title: ⚡ Quick Fix (Terminal)
docs.text:
Remove the quarantine flag:

xattr -cr /Applications/Flocon.app

docs.title: 🛠️ Manual Authorization (System Settings)
docs.text:
If you prefer to authorize through the macOS UI:

  1. Attempt Launch: Move Flocon.app to your /Applications folder and open it. macOS will warn that it cannot be opened.

  2. Open Help: Click the ? icon in the dialog.

  3. Open Privacy Settings: Click the link "Open Privacy & Security for me".

  4. Click Open Anyway: Scroll down to the Security section and click Open Anyway.

  5. Confirm Launch: Click Open Anyway in the confirmation dialog and authenticate with your password or Touch ID.

Flocon Desktop is now permanently authorized on your Mac!

docs.title: 📱 Android: adb
docs.text:
To reach Android emulators and USB devices, Flocon Desktop needs adb in your PATH. It comes with the Android SDK platform-tools (installed with Android Studio), or with Homebrew:

brew install --cask android-platform-tools

Next: add the SDK to your app.

docs.title: 🍳 MCP Cookbook
docs.text:
Ten workflows you can copy. Each one gives the goal, the prompt you type, the tool calls the agent makes (in order, with the key arguments), a short result and some tips.

About the results

The results shown are illustrative: urls, ids, values and wording depend on your app and on your agent. The tool names and arguments are the real ones, see the Tools Reference.

Before you start: Flocon Desktop is running, your agent is connected, and your app is connected to Flocon. By default the tools use the device and app selected in Flocon Desktop (see targeting).

docs.title: 1. Why does this request fail
docs.text:
Goal: understand a failing call, and get a command to replay it yourself.

Prompt

My article page doesn't display. Is it a network call? If so, give me the cURL.

Tool calls

  1. list_network_calls with onlyErrors: true, limit: 20: the failed calls of the current session.
  2. get_network_call with callId: "<id of the failing call>": headers, bodies, error and cURL (includeCurl is true by default).

Result (illustrative)

GET /articles/42 failed with 500 Internal Server Error in 312 ms.
Response body: {"error":"article_service_unavailable"}
The request has the header Authorization: Bearer eyJ... (valid format).

curl -X GET 'https://api.example.com/articles/42' -H 'Authorization: Bearer eyJ...'

Tips

  • The agent starts from summaries and only opens the calls it needs: bodies can be large.
  • To search for a value anywhere (a header, a field of a body), ask for it: the agent uses search_network_calls with query.
  • Replaying the cURL in your terminal tells you if the error comes from the server or from what your app sends.

docs.title: 2. Mock an endpoint to test an error state
docs.text:
Goal: see how a screen behaves on a server error, without touching the backend.

Prompt

Make the articles endpoint fail with a 500 so I can check my error screen. Tell me when it's on, and turn it off at the end.

Tool calls

  1. list_network_calls with urlContains: "/articles", limit: 5: finds a real captured call.
  2. create_network_mock with fromCallId: "<id>", httpCode: 500, body: "{\"error\":\"internal_error\"}", displayName: "Articles 500": copies url, method and response from the call, and overrides the status and body. Active right away.
  3. You open an article in the app and check the error screen.
  4. update_network_mock with mockId: "<id>", enabled: false: stops the mock without deleting it.

Result (illustrative)

Mock "Articles 500" created for GET .*/articles/.* : status 500, enabled.
...
Mock "Articles 500" is now disabled (kept in Flocon, you can enable it again).

Tips

  • Mock a network failure instead of an HTTP error with exceptionClassPath: "java.net.SocketTimeoutException" (no httpCode).
  • Add delayMs to also test the loading state.
  • shared: true applies the mock to all your apps and devices: leave it off unless you want that.
  • Agents are told to prefer disabling over deleting, and to tell you which mocks are still enabled. See Mocking.

docs.title: 3. Reproduce a slow or flaky network
docs.text:
Goal: check loading states, timeouts and retries on a bad connection.

Prompt

Make my network slow (2 to 5 seconds) and flaky (30% of calls fail with a timeout or a 503). I'll navigate the app, then tell you when to stop.

Tool calls

  1. list_bad_network_configs: reuses an existing config if there is one.
  2. create_bad_network_config with name: "Slow and flaky", latencyTriggerProbability: 1, minLatencyMs: 2000, maxLatencyMs: 5000, errorProbability: 0.3, errors: [{"exceptionClassPath": "java.net.SocketTimeoutException"}, {"httpCode": 503, "body": "{\"error\":\"unavailable\"}"}], enabled: true.
  3. You use the app. Then the agent can read the effect: list_network_calls with sinceTimestamp: <time you started>, to see durations and failures.
  4. set_active_bad_network_config with no configId: turns the simulation off, the config is kept.

Result (illustrative)

Active config: "Slow and flaky".
Since then: 41 calls, 12 failed (7 SocketTimeoutException, 5 with a 503), median duration 3.4 s.
The feed screen shows no error state after a 503: the list stays empty.
Simulation is now off.

Tips

  • Asking the agent to look at the calls afterwards gives you evidence of what the user experienced, not only what you saw.
  • Combine with workflow 8 to record the screen while the network is bad.
  • Always finish with the simulation off: agents are told to do it and to say which config they left active. See Bad network.

docs.title: 4. Inspect the database after an action
docs.text:
Goal: check that what the user did was really saved, and with the right values.

Prompt

I just created an account in the app. Is the user saved in the database with the right email?

Tool calls

  1. list_databases: gives the databaseId.
  2. list_database_tables with databaseId: "<id>": the schema, to find the right table and columns.
  3. query_database with databaseId: "<id>", sql: "SELECT id, email, created_at FROM users ORDER BY created_at DESC LIMIT 3".
  4. Optional: list_database_query_logs with databaseId: "<id>", text: "users", to see the queries your app ran, if query logging is set up.

Result (illustrative)

users, 1 row matches: id=18, email="jean@example.com", created_at="2026-11-03 14:31:55".
The email is saved as typed, but without trimming: the input had a trailing space.

Tips

  • Only read-only SQL runs (SELECT, PRAGMA, EXPLAIN). Always keep a LIMIT: the app sends all the rows.
  • Preferences work the same way: list_shared_preferences, then get_shared_preference_values with sharedPreferenceId and an optional text filter.
  • Query logs show transactions: pass a transactionId from a previous result to see only one.

docs.title: 5. Crash triage
docs.text:
Goal: find the cause of a crash from what the app did just before.

Prompt

The app just crashed. What happened in the two minutes before?

Tool calls

  1. get_timeline with no argument: it anchors on the latest crash and says why. To be explicit: mode: "before_crash".
  2. get_crash_report with crashId: "<id of the crash line, after crash:>": the full stack trace.
  3. get_network_call with callId: "<id of a suspicious line, after network:>" if a call looks wrong.
  4. Optional: show_in_timeline with no argument, to open the zone around the crash in Flocon Desktop for you.

Result (illustrative)

Window: 14:31:05 to 14:32:10 (the minute before the latest crash, plus 5 s). 38 events, 3 anomalies:
- crash:c91  IllegalStateException: "token is null"  (14:32:05)
- network:a7 POST /v1/checkout -> 401  (14:32:03)
- 12x GET /v1/feed in 3.1 s  (14:31:48, loop)
The 401 happened 2 s before the crash, and the stack trace points to CheckoutViewModel.pay().

Tips

  • The times are those of the phone, not your computer. Give times as HH:mm and the tool uses the phone clock; the answer shows the window it chose.
  • Read the window and the notes in the answer before concluding: an empty timeline can mean the window was wrong.
  • To check whether something was sent at all, use search: get_timeline with search: "checkout_failed" returns found and never cuts the matches.
  • excludeSources: ["database"] removes noisy transactions.
  • See Timeline and Crash reporter.

docs.title: 6. Toggle a feature flag and verify the calls change
docs.text:
Goal: check that flipping a flag really changes what the app does.

Flocon shows feature flags but does not change them: you flip the flag in your provider (Firebase, Statsig, your own debug menu...), the agent checks the effect.

Prompt

I'm going to turn new_checkout on in our provider. Read the flag now, tell me when to flip it, then compare the network calls of the checkout before and after.

Tool calls

  1. get_feature_flag with provider: "firebase", name: "new_checkout": state, variant and payload before.
  2. list_network_calls with urlContains: "/checkout": the calls before (note the time of the latest one).
  3. You flip the flag, restart or refresh the app, and run the checkout again.
  4. get_feature_flag again: confirms the new variant.
  5. list_network_calls with urlContains: "/checkout", sinceTimestamp: <time of the flip>: the calls after.

Result (illustrative)

new_checkout (firebase): off -> treatment, payload {"steps":3}.
Before: POST /v1/checkout (1 call). After: POST /v2/checkout/init, POST /v2/checkout/confirm (2 calls).
The new flow is used, and /v1/checkout is no longer called.

Tips

  • Use list_feature_flags with query: "checkout" if you do not know the exact name or provider.
  • To compare two flows, ask the agent to put the two lists in a table.
  • See Feature flags.

docs.title: 7. Accessibility audit by moving the focus
docs.text:
Goal: check what TalkBack reads, screen by screen, in the focus order. Android only: the focus tools need TalkBack and adb.

Prompt

TalkBack is on. Walk through the focus order of the profile screen and tell me every element without a content description.

Turn TalkBack on yourself on the device first: the agent cannot do that for you.

Tool calls

  1. get_accessibility_state: is capture supported, is a screen reader running.
  2. clear_accessibility_events: starts from an empty list.
  3. get_accessibility_focused_node: where the focus is now.
  4. move_accessibility_focus with direction: "next", repeated: each call returns the element it landed on.
  5. list_accessibility_events with type: "VIEW_FOCUSED", limit: 50: everything TalkBack received.

Result (illustrative)

Focus order of the profile screen (9 stops):
1. "Back" button  2. "Jean Dupont" heading  3. ImageButton (no content description)
4. "Follow" button ...
Problem: stop 3 is an ImageButton with no text and no content description, TalkBack would read "button".

Tips

  • move_accessibility_focus does not wrap around: the agent stops when the focus does not move.
  • If list_accessibility_events is empty, get_accessibility_state tells why (no screen reader, capture not supported).
  • On iOS, the Swift and Flutter SDKs do not send accessibility events yet. See Accessibility.

docs.title: 8. Capture a screenshot and a recording of a bug for a ticket
docs.text:
Goal: attach proof to a bug report.

Prompt

Record me opening the cart and paying, stop when I tell you, then take a screenshot and list the failed calls for the ticket.

Tool calls

  1. start_screen_recording.
  2. You reproduce the bug.
  3. take_screenshot: saved as a PNG in Screenshot/, and the image is returned so the agent can see the screen.
  4. stop_screen_recording: saved as an mp4 in ScreenRecord/.
  5. list_network_calls with onlyErrors: true and sinceTimestamp: <start time>: the failed calls during the recording.
  6. Optional: open_flocon_folder with subfolder: "ScreenRecord": opens the folder on your computer.

Result (illustrative)

Recording saved: ~/Documents/Flocon/ScreenRecord/record_com.example.shop_1736000000000.mp4
Screenshot saved in ~/Documents/Flocon/Screenshot/ (PNG).
The screenshot shows an empty payment form with no message. POST /payments returned 402 during the recording.

Tips

  • Uses adb on Android and the booted Simulator on iOS. Not available for a device connected over Wi-Fi.
  • One recording per device, and on Android screenrecord stops by itself after 3 minutes.
  • Ask the agent to write the ticket text from what it saw, and attach the two files yourself.

docs.title: 9. Open a deeplink and check the network calls and the screen
docs.text:
Goal: check that a deeplink lands on the right screen and loads the right data.

Prompt

Open the deeplink for the profile of user 42 on the posts tab. Then tell me what screen it shows and which calls it made.

Tool calls

  1. list_deeplinks: the deeplinks declared by the app, with their parameters.
  2. open_deeplink with link: "myapp://profile/42?tab=posts", deeplinkId: <id from list_deeplinks> (keeps the label in the history).
  3. take_screenshot: the agent looks at the screen.
  4. list_network_calls with sinceTimestamp: <time just before the deeplink>: the calls it triggered.

Result (illustrative)

Deeplink opened. The screen shows the profile of "Marie" with the Posts tab selected.
Calls since: GET /users/42 -> 200 (180 ms), GET /users/42/posts?limit=20 -> 200 (240 ms).

Tips

  • Fill every parameter of the link before opening it.
  • Android uses adb, iOS the booted Simulator.
  • list_deeplink_history shows what was already opened from Flocon. See Deeplinks.

docs.title: 10. Install Flocon in an existing project
docs.text:
Goal: add Flocon to an app (Kotlin, Swift or Flutter), or migrate it from 1.x, with the agent doing the edits.

This one uses the flocon-setup skill of the Flocon plugin, not the MCP tools. Install the plugin first, see Install with the Flocon plugin.

Prompt

Set up Flocon in this project. I want network and database, and it must not be in release builds.

What the agent does

  1. Detects the platform from the project files: Android (com.android.application), Kotlin Multiplatform, Swift (.xcodeproj, Package.swift) or Flutter (pubspec.yaml).
  2. Detects the version if Flocon is already there, and picks a path: install, migrate from 1.x to 2.0, or only add the missing plugins.
  3. Adds the dependencies following the matching setup: Kotlin (debug module, -no-op twin for release), Swift Package Manager (FloconSwift), or flutter pub add flocon and the plugin packages.
  4. Starts Flocon in the app, and installs only the plugins the project really uses (it searches the code instead of guessing).
  5. Keeps it out of release: it inspects the real build variants and tells you exactly what it did (SDK inactive vs absent from the binary).
  6. Builds the touched targets and says what was not verified (running on a device, connection to Flocon Desktop, release build).

Result (illustrative)

Kotlin SDK 2.0: added flocon (debug) and flocon-no-op (release), network and database plugins.
Compiled debug and release. Not verified: the app running on a device and showing in Flocon Desktop.

Tips

  • Then run the app with Flocon Desktop open, and ask: "List my network calls". If a tool returns nothing, the agent can tell which wiring is missing.
  • The skill follows the docs of each SDK: if the skill and the docs disagree, the docs win, and it tells you.
  • It works on a branch and does not touch your unrelated uncommitted changes.
  • See Install with the Flocon plugin and Migrating from 1.x.

docs.title: 🧰 MCP Tools Reference
docs.text:
The Flocon MCP server exposes 57 tools. This page lists all of them, by area. For the setup of your agent, see Overview & Setup. For tools chained together on real problems, see the Cookbook.

Your agent discovers the tools and their parameters by itself (the server describes each one), so you rarely need this page to use them. It is useful to know what an agent can and cannot do, and to write precise prompts.

docs.title: Legend
docs.text:
Badge Meaning Read-only Reads what Flocon captured. Nothing changes. Side effect Changes something: the behavior of your app, the device, Flocon Desktop or your computer. The kind of change is written next to the badge.

In the parameter tables, Req. is ✅ when the parameter is required. Types are JSON types: string, integer, number, boolean, array, object. Limits and defaults come from the tool schema.

docs.title: Targeting: deviceId and packageName
docs.text:
Most tools act on one app on one device. By default, that is the device and app currently selected in Flocon Desktop. To act on another one, call list_devices then pass deviceId and packageName.

Tools that take these two optional parameters are marked Targets: device / app and the two parameters are not repeated in their tables.

You pass Flocon targets Nothing The device and app selected in Flocon Desktop. If nothing is selected, the call fails and lists the available targets. packageName only That app on the selected device, otherwise on the device where it was seen most recently. deviceId only The app selected on that device, otherwise its only app. If the device has several apps, the call fails and lists their package names. Both Exactly that app on that device.

packageName is the Android package name or the iOS bundle id.

Wi-Fi devices

A device connected over Wi-Fi has connectionType: wifi in list_devices. Tools that use adb (screenshot, recording, deeplink) are not available for it.

docs.title: Platform notes
docs.text:
• Android: tools that act on the device (screenshot, recording, deeplink, accessibility focus) use adb.
  • iOS: screenshot, recording and deeplink use the booted Simulator. Physical iOS devices are not supported for these.
  • Data tools return what the SDK of your app sends. If your SDK does not send a kind of data, the tool is still there but returns nothing. See the platform support matrix.

docs.title: list_devices
docs.text:
Read-only

Lists the devices and apps known by Flocon, the one currently selected in Flocon Desktop (used by default by the other tools), whether each app is connected, and each device's connectionType (default or wifi). Parameters: none.

docs.title: list_network_calls
docs.text:
Read-only · Targets: device / app

Lists the network calls (HTTP, GraphQL, gRPC, WebSocket events), newest first, as summaries (no headers, no bodies). By default only the current app session (since the last launch).

Parameter Type Req. Description text string Full text filter: url, method, status, duration, bodies. urlContains string Only calls whose url contains this text (case insensitive). methods array of string Only these methods, e.g. ["GET", "POST"]. statusCodes array of integer Only these HTTP status codes, e.g. [401, 500]. onlyErrors boolean Only failed calls: exceptions, HTTP code >= 400, GraphQL errors, gRPC status != OK. Default false. type string http, graphql, grpc or websocket. sinceTimestamp integer Only calls started after this epoch timestamp (ms). includeOldSessions boolean Include previous app launches. Default false. order string newest_first (default) or oldest_first. limit integer 1 to 500. Default 50.

docs.title: get_network_call
docs.text:
Read-only · Targets: device / app

Full details of one call: request and response headers and bodies, GraphQL query, gRPC status, error, timing, and the equivalent cURL command.

Parameter Type Req. Description callId string ✅ Id from list_network_calls or search_network_calls. maxBodyChars integer Bodies longer than this are truncated. 100 to 200000. Default 20000. includeCurl boolean Include the cURL command. Default true.

docs.title: search_network_calls
docs.text:
Read-only · Targets: device / app

Searches a text in the headers, bodies, url, method and status of the captured calls, including previous app sessions by default. Returns summaries, newest first.

Parameter Type Req. Description query string ✅ Text to search, case insensitive. scopes array of string Where to search. Default: everywhere. includeOldSessions boolean Default true. limit integer 1 to 500. Default 50.

docs.title: Mocks
docs.text: Mocks make the app receive a fake response (or throw an exception) instead of calling the server. They apply immediately when the app is connected to Flocon. See Mocking.

docs.title: list_network_mocks
docs.text:
Read-only · Targets: device / app

Lists the mocks of the app, including the ones shared with all apps. Bodies are not returned.

Parameter Type Req. Description onlyEnabled boolean Only enabled mocks. Default false.

docs.title: get_network_mock
docs.text:
Read-only

All the details of a mock, including the mocked body and headers.

Parameter Type Req. Description mockId string ✅ Id from list_network_mocks. maxBodyChars integer Truncation limit. 100 to 200000. Default 20000.

docs.title: create_network_mock
docs.text:
Side effect: app behavior · Targets: device / app

Creates a mock. Start from a captured call with fromCallId (url, method and response are copied), then override what you need, for example only httpCode to simulate a server error.

Parameter Type Req. Description fromCallId string Id of a captured call used as a template. urlPattern string Regex that must match the whole url, query included. E.g. .*/users/[0-9]+. method string HTTP method, or * for any. displayName string Name displayed in Flocon. httpCode integer Status of the mocked response, 100 to 599. Default 200. body string Body of the mocked response. mediaType string Media type of the body. headers object Headers of the mocked response, e.g. {"Cache-Control": "no-cache"}. delayMs integer Delay before the response, in ms. Default 0. exceptionClassPath string Instead of a response, the request throws this exception, e.g. java.net.SocketTimeoutException. enabled boolean Whether the mock is active. Default true. shared boolean Apply to all devices and apps. Default false.

docs.title: update_network_mock
docs.text:
Side effect: app behavior · deviceId / packageName move the mock

Changes only the given fields. Use enabled to enable or disable it. Giving exceptionClassPath turns it into an exception mock, giving httpCode, body, mediaType or headers turns it into a body mock.

Parameter Type Req. Description mockId string ✅ Id from list_network_mocks. urlPattern, method, displayName, httpCode, body, mediaType, headers, delayMs, exceptionClassPath Same as create_network_mock. enabled boolean Enable or disable the mock. shared boolean Share with all apps, or only one app. deviceId, packageName string Moves the mock to this device / app. By default it stays on its app.

docs.title: delete_network_mock
docs.text:
Side effect: app behavior

Deletes a mock. To stop it temporarily, prefer update_network_mock with enabled: false.

Parameter Type Req. Description mockId string ✅ Id from list_network_mocks.

docs.title: list_websocket_clients
docs.text:
Read-only · Targets: device / app

Lists the ids of the app's WebSockets that accept injected messages. Only the Android SDK (OkHttp FloconWebSocket) registers them for now. Parameters: none besides targeting.

docs.title: send_websocket_message
docs.text:
Side effect: app behavior · Targets: device / app

Injects a text message into a WebSocket of the app, as if it was received from the server. Android OkHttp only for now.

Parameter Type Req. Description websocketId string ✅ Id from list_websocket_clients. message string ✅ Text received by the app, e.g. a JSON payload.

docs.title: Bad network
docs.text: A bad network config simulates a poor connection: a part of the requests are delayed, a part fail with an error response or an exception. Only one config is active at a time. See Bad network.

docs.title: list_bad_network_configs
docs.text:
Read-only · Targets: device / app

Lists the configs of the app and which one is active. Parameters: none besides targeting.

docs.title: create_bad_network_config
docs.text:
Side effect: app behavior · Targets: device / app

Creates a config. Not active until enabled: true or set_active_bad_network_config. For example, a slow network is latencyTriggerProbability: 1, minLatencyMs: 2000, maxLatencyMs: 5000.

Parameter Type Req. Description name string ✅ Name displayed in Flocon. latencyTriggerProbability number Chance from 0 to 1 that a request is delayed. Default 0. minLatencyMs integer Minimum added latency, in ms. Default 0. maxLatencyMs integer Maximum added latency, in ms. Default 0. errorProbability number Chance from 0 to 1 that a request fails (needs at least one error). Default 0. errors array of object Possible errors, one is picked by weight. Each: weight (default 1), httpCode or exceptionClassPath, body, contentType. enabled boolean Also activates it now, deactivating the others. Default false.

docs.title: update_bad_network_config
docs.text:
Side effect: app behavior · Targets: device / app

Changes only the given fields. An update of the active config applies right away. To activate or deactivate, use set_active_bad_network_config.

Parameter Type Req. Description configId string ✅ Id from list_bad_network_configs. name, latencyTriggerProbability, minLatencyMs, maxLatencyMs, errorProbability Same as create_bad_network_config. errors array of object Replaces all the existing errors.

docs.title: set_active_bad_network_config
docs.text:
Side effect: app behavior · Targets: device / app

Activates a config (the others are deactivated), or turns the simulation off when configId is omitted.

Parameter Type Req. Description configId string Config to activate. Omit to turn the simulation off.

docs.title: delete_bad_network_config
docs.text:
Side effect: app behavior · Targets: device / app

Deletes a config. If it was active, the simulation is turned off.

Parameter Type Req. Description configId string ✅ Id from list_bad_network_configs.

docs.title: Database
docs.text: The app must be connected to Flocon. Only read-only SQL runs. See Database.

docs.title: list_databases
docs.text:
Read-only · Targets: device / app

Lists the SQLite databases of the app (Room, SQLDelight...), with the databaseId used by the other database tools. Parameters: none besides targeting.

docs.title: list_database_tables
docs.text:
Read-only · Targets: device / app

Schema of a database: tables, columns, types, primary keys.

Parameter Type Req. Description databaseId string ✅ Id from list_databases.

docs.title: query_database
docs.text:
Read-only · Targets: device / app

Runs a read-only SQL query (SELECT, PRAGMA without value, EXPLAIN) and returns the rows. Statements that modify the database are refused. Add a LIMIT: the app sends all the rows.

Parameter Type Req. Description databaseId string ✅ Id from list_databases. sql string ✅ SQLite query, e.g. SELECT * FROM users WHERE id = 3. maxRows integer 1 to 1000. Default 100. maxCellChars integer Longer values are truncated. 10 to 100000. Default 1000.

docs.title: list_database_query_logs
docs.text:
Read-only · Targets: device / app

Lists the SQL queries executed by the app, newest first, with their arguments. Only available when the app logs its queries to Flocon (see query logging). Each query has a transactionId when it ran in a transaction.

Parameter Type Req. Description databaseId string ✅ Id from list_databases. text string Only queries containing this text, in the SQL or the arguments. includeTransactions boolean Include BEGIN / COMMIT / ROLLBACK. Default false. includeOldSessions boolean Include previous app launches. Default false. transactionId string Only the queries of this transaction. limit integer 1 to 1000. Default 100.

docs.title: Preferences
docs.text: See Preferences.

docs.title: list_shared_preferences
docs.text:
Read-only · Targets: device / app

Lists the SharedPreferences files (Android) and UserDefaults suites (iOS), with their sharedPreferenceId and storage type (SharedPreferences, DataStore, UserDefaults, Keychain...). Parameters: none besides targeting.

docs.title: get_shared_preference_values
docs.text:
Read-only · Targets: device / app

Keys and typed values of one file, as stored.

Parameter Type Req. Description sharedPreferenceId string ✅ Id from list_shared_preferences. text string Only entries containing this text in the key or value. limit integer 1 to 1000. Default 100.

docs.title: set_shared_preference_value
docs.text:
Side effect: app data (destructive) · Targets: device / app

Edits the value of one existing key. Keys cannot be created or removed. It is the only tool that edits captured data. It returns the previous value and whether the app confirmed the edit. The server asks agents to read the value first and to get your confirmation.

Parameter Type Req. Description sharedPreferenceId string ✅ Id from list_shared_preferences. key string ✅ An existing key. value string ✅ New value, as text, exactly of the right type: "12" for an int, "true" for a boolean, a JSON array of strings for a string_set. type string string, int, long, float, boolean or string_set. Default: the type of the current value.

docs.title: Files
docs.text: Browse the app's sandbox. The app must be connected to Flocon, otherwise the last known content is returned. See Files.

docs.title: list_file_roots
docs.text:
Read-only · Targets: device / app

Lists the root folders announced by the app (id, name, absolute path): the platform defaults (files and caches on Android; documents, caches and tmp on iOS) and the folders registered by the app. Parameters: none besides targeting.

docs.title: list_files
docs.text:
Read-only · Targets: device / app

Lists a directory: name, absolute path, size, last modification.

Parameter Type Req. Description path string A root folder id from list_file_roots, or the absolute path of a directory. Default: the first root.

docs.title: read_file
docs.text:
Read-only · Targets: device / app

Downloads a file: text files (json, xml, logs...) as text, images as images, only metadata for other binary files. A copy is saved on your computer (localPath); the file in the app is not touched.

Parameter Type Req. Description path string ✅ Absolute path, from list_files. maxChars integer Text longer than this is truncated. 100 to 200000. Default 20000.

docs.title: list_images
docs.text:
Read-only · Targets: device / app

Images loaded by the app (url, load time), newest first. Only the url is known, not the image content.

Parameter Type Req. Description text string Only images whose url contains this text. sinceTimestamp integer Only images loaded after this epoch timestamp (ms). includeHeaders boolean Include the response headers. docs.title: list_analytics_tables
docs.text:
Read-only · Targets: device / app

Lists the analytics tables: one per analytics SDK or tracker sending events to Flocon. Parameters: none besides targeting.

docs.title: list_analytics_events
docs.text:
Read-only · Targets: device / app

Events with their properties, newest first. By default only the current app session, from all tables.

Parameter Type Req. Description analyticsTableId string Only this table (from list_analytics_tables). eventNames array of string Only events with one of these exact names. text string Only events containing this text in name, date or properties. sinceTimestamp integer Only events after this epoch timestamp (ms). includeOldSessions boolean Default false. order string newest_first (default) or oldest_first. limit integer 1 to 500. Default 50.

docs.title: count_analytics_events
docs.text:
Read-only · Targets: device / app

Number of events per event name, the most frequent first. Same filters as list_analytics_events: analyticsTableId, eventNames, text, sinceTimestamp, includeOldSessions (no order, no limit).

docs.title: Feature flags
docs.text: See Feature flags.

docs.title: list_feature_flags
docs.text:
Read-only · Targets: device / app

Flags with provider, name, state (on, off or custom), evaluated variant and a payload preview.

Parameter Type Req. Description provider string Only this provider, e.g. firebase. query string Only flags whose name, variant or payload contains this text. limit integer 1 to 500. Default 100.

docs.title: get_feature_flag
docs.text:
Read-only · Targets: device / app

One flag with its state, variant and full payload.

Parameter Type Req. Description provider string ✅ Provider of the flag (from list_feature_flags). name string ✅ Name of the flag.

Note

Agents read flags, they do not change them. To flip a flag, use the Flocon Desktop screen or your provider.

docs.title: list_tables
docs.text:

Lists the custom tables sent by the app (Table plugin), with their tableId. Parameters: none besides targeting.

docs.title: list_table_items
docs.text:
Read-only · Targets: device / app

Rows of a table, newest first, each row being a column to value map.

docs.title: list_dashboards
docs.text:
Read-only · Targets: device / app

Ids of the dashboards sent by the app, and the one selected in Flocon Desktop. Parameters: none besides targeting.

docs.title: get_dashboard
docs.text:
Read-only · Targets: device / app

A dashboard with its containers and elements (texts, values, check boxes, text fields, buttons), as the app last sent it. Nothing is triggered: buttons and fields cannot be used by an agent.

Parameter Type Req. Description dashboardId string Id from list_dashboards. Default: the dashboard selected in Flocon Desktop.

docs.title: Deeplinks
docs.text: See Deeplinks.

docs.title: list_deeplinks
docs.text:
Read-only · Targets: device / app

Deeplinks declared by the app (link, label, description, parameters) and the variables their parameters can use. Parameters: none besides targeting.

docs.title: list_deeplink_history
docs.text:
Read-only · Targets: device / app

Deeplinks recently opened from Flocon, with the parameters used. Parameters: none besides targeting.

docs.title: open_deeplink
docs.text:
Side effect: device · Targets: device / app

Opens a deeplink in the app: adb on Android, the booted Simulator on iOS. Not available for Android devices connected over Wi-Fi. Fill all the parameters of the link first (see list_deeplinks).

Parameter Type Req. Description link string ✅ Full deeplink with its parameters filled, e.g. myapp://profile/42?tab=posts. deeplinkId integer Id of a declared deeplink, to keep its label in the history. saveIntoHistory boolean Add to the Flocon history. Default true.

docs.title: Timeline
docs.text: See Timeline.

docs.title: get_timeline
docs.text:
Read-only · Targets: device / app

What the app did in a window of time, above the network: every source (network, database, analytics, crashes, deeplinks, logs, accessibility, WebView...) in one narrative. One line per event with an id (source:id), repetitions folded (12× GET /feed in 3 s), anomalies first (crash, HTTP errors, ERROR logs, calls in a loop, large responses). Give nothing and it anchors on the latest crash, otherwise on the last 2 minutes of the latest session, and the answer says which window and why. The times are those of the phone.

Each line id works with the matching tool: network:<callId> with get_network_call, crash:<crashId> with get_crash_report.

Parameter Type Req. Description mode string recent (last minutes), session, before_crash, at, range. Omit to let the tool choose. at string Time for mode at: epoch ms, ISO-8601 with an offset (2026-11-03T14:32:00+01:00), or HH:mm[:ss]. from string Start of mode range, same formats. to string End of mode range, same formats. Defaults to the last event. eventId string An event id of a previous answer (network:abc): reads around it. Not with mode, at, from, to. aroundSeconds integer Half width of the window for at and eventId. Default 30. minutes integer Length for mode recent. Default 5. search string Text to look for in the window (name, url, query...). Matches are never cut, and found tells if the event was sent. searchSource string Only search in this source. sources array of string Only read these sources: network, database, analytics, accessibility, webview, crash, table, deeplink, adb. excludeSources array of string Leave these sources out, e.g. ["database"]. maxLines integer 1 to 400. Default 150. Database lines are the first dropped when capped.

docs.title: show_in_timeline
docs.text:
Side effect: Flocon Desktop · Targets: device / app

Shows a zone of the timeline in the Flocon Desktop window for you: opens the timeline, selects the device and app, selects an event and centers the graph on its zone. Flocon is not brought to the front, so the agent asks you to go to the Flocon window. Your filters are never changed: if one hides the event, the answer says which. The graph draws network, database and analytics events only: a crash is shown with its zone, and its row is in the list view.

Parameter Type Req. Description eventId string An event id of get_timeline. Not with mode, at, from, to. mode, at, from, to Same as get_timeline. aroundSeconds integer Half width of the zone shown. Default 30. view string graph (default) or list. Changes the timeline view saved in your preferences.

With nothing given, it shows the latest crash, otherwise the main anomaly of the last 2 minutes.

docs.title: list_crash_reports

Read-only · Targets: device / app

Accessibility events (focus, announcements, content changes) with text, content description, class and screen, newest first.

Whether automatic capture is supported and enabled, whether a screen reader is running, touch exploration, and the running services. Use it when list_accessibility_events is empty. Parameters: none besides targeting.

docs.title: get_accessibility_focused_node
docs.text:

docs.title: move_accessibility_focus
docs.text:
Side effect: device · Targets: device / app

Moves the accessibility focus to the next or previous element, like a TalkBack swipe, and returns the element it landed on. Android only, needs TalkBack on.

docs.title: clear_accessibility_events
docs.text:

Deletes the accessibility events received from the app, to isolate the events of the next interaction. Parameters: none besides targeting.

docs.title: list_webview_events
docs.text:
Read-only · Targets: device / app

What happened in the app's WebViews, newest first: JS console messages, page events (loads, navigation, errors) and calls from the page to a native object (bridge). Requests made by the page are in the network tools. The Swift and Flutter SDKs do not send WebView events yet. See WebView.

Parameter Type Req. Description kind string console, page or bridge. All by default. text string Only events containing this text in level / type, message, url or WebView id. sinceTimestamp integer Only events after this epoch timestamp (ms). order string newest_first (default) or oldest_first. limit integer 1 to 500. Default 50.

docs.title: take_screenshot

docs.text:
Side effect: device · Targets: device

docs.title: flocon_navigate_into_desktop_app
docs.text:
Side effect: Flocon Desktop

Moves the Flocon Desktop window for you: displays a screen, selects a device and app, sets the timeline view. This changes what you selected in Flocon. Flocon is not brought to the front, so the agent asks you to go to the Flocon window. At least one parameter is required, and nothing changes if one is invalid.

Description screen string dashboard, network, images, database, files, shared_preferences, analytics, feature_flags, accessibility, tables, deeplinks, adb_commander, crash_reporter, timeline, web_view. deviceId string Selects this device in Flocon. packageName string Selects this app (and its device if different). timelineView string graph or list. docs.title: take_flocon_desktop_screenshot
docs.text:
Read-only

Returns an image of what the Flocon Desktop window currently displays (not the device screen: use take_screenshot for that). Only the visible content is captured, scaled down if too big, and nothing is saved on your computer. Parameters: none.

docs.title: get_server_ports
docs.text:
Read-only

Ports of the Flocon Desktop servers the SDKs connect to: the websocket (default 9023) and HTTP (default 9024) ports. Returns the effective ports, the saved ones, the defaults, whether each is forced by a launch option (--websocket-port, --http-port or the FLOCON_WEBSOCKET_PORT, FLOCON_HTTP_PORT environment variables), and the MCP port. Parameters: none.

docs.title: set_server_ports
docs.text:
Side effect: Flocon Desktop

Changes the websocket and / or HTTP port (saved in the Flocon settings). The omitted one keeps its value, and 9023 / 9024 put the defaults back. Ports must be in 1024..65535 and different, not 9042 (reserved for MCP), the websocket port cannot be 9024 and the HTTP port cannot be 9023. A port forced by a launch option cannot be changed.

Warning

Applying the ports restarts the websocket and HTTP servers and disconnects every device until the SDKs reconnect with the new ports. The MCP server on 9042 is not affected, and it cannot be moved.

Parameter Type Req. Description websocketPort integer New websocket port. httpPort integer New HTTP port.

docs.text:

Opens the Flocon documents folder (screenshots, screen recordings, exports) in the file manager and returns its path.

docs.title: 🤖 AI Agents (MCP)
docs.text:
Flocon Desktop embeds an MCP server (Model Context Protocol). Once your AI coding agent is connected to it, the agent sees what you see in Flocon, without any copy / paste, and can act on your running app.

"List the failed calls of the last launch and explain why the login fails"

"Make the login call return a 500 so I can check the error screen"

"What happened in the app just before it crashed?"

docs.title: What your agent gets
docs.text:
It can see everything Flocon captured from the connected app: the network calls (HTTP, GraphQL, gRPC, WebSocket) with bodies and a ready cURL, the databases, the preferences, the app files, the analytics events, the feature flags, the crashes, the images, the accessibility and WebView events, the dashboards and tables, and a single timeline of what the app did around a moment.

It can act:

  • On app behavior: create and edit network mocks, simulate a bad network, inject a WebSocket message, edit the value of an existing preference key.
  • On the device: open a deeplink, take a screenshot, record the screen, move the accessibility focus.
  • On Flocon Desktop: show a zone of the timeline or a screen in the window, change the server ports.

All the tools are listed in the Tools Reference, and real workflows are in the Cookbook.

Local only

The MCP server listens on 127.0.0.1 only: it is not reachable from your local network. It has no authentication, so any program running on your computer can call it while Flocon Desktop is open.

Captured data is read-only: an agent cannot modify, delete or replay network calls, files, databases, analytics events, feature flags or crashes. The one exception is the value of an existing preference key, with set_shared_preference_value. Only read-only SQL (SELECT, PRAGMA without value, EXPLAIN) runs on databases.

Every tool is flagged read-only or not in the Tools Reference, and agents are told to name what they changed (mocks left enabled, active bad network config...). Flocon only counts, anonymously, which tool is called and the kind of client: see Telemetry.

docs.title: Which apps feed which data
docs.text:
The tools are the same for every SDK, but each tool returns what your app's SDK sends. An empty answer for a feature your app does not use is normal, not a bug.

Data Kotlin (Android / KMP) Swift Flutter Network, mocks, bad network ✅ ✅ (instrumented URLSessions) ✅ (Dio, package:http) Databases, preferences, files ✅ ✅ ✅ Analytics, feature flags, tables, dashboards, deeplinks, images ✅ ✅ ✅ Timeline logs, crashes ✅ ✅ ✅ (Dart and Flutter errors) WebView events, accessibility events ✅ ❌ ❌ WebSocket message injection ✅ (OkHttp) ❌ ❌

See the platform support matrix for the details per feature. Screenshots, recordings and deeplinks need adb on Android, or a booted Simulator on iOS.

docs.title: Setup
docs.text:
Flocon Desktop must be running. The server starts with it and listens on:

http://localhost:9042/mcp
